title: The Strongest Evidence Against God Isn't Science
description:
Most people think the strongest arguments against God come from science, evolution, the Big Bang, cosmology, or physics. But what if the biggest evidence against God's existence is religion itself?

In this video, we explore a simple but powerful question: If one God created all human beings, why do we have thousands of religions, sects, scriptures, and contradictory claims? Why do religious groups constantly disagree about prophets, salvation, holy books, and divine truth?

Using everyday examples, common-sense reasoning, and the analogy of a parent dealing with children, this video examines whether religion makes more sense as a human creation than a divine message.

We also discuss religious institutions, donations, temples, churches, mosques, and the role of money in organized religion. If God is all-powerful, why does religion so often resemble human organizations competing for influence, authority, and followers?

This is not a discussion about science versus religion. It is a discussion about whether religion itself raises difficult questions about the existence of God.

If you've searched for atheism, religion, God, evidence against God, strongest argument against God, why religion exists, does God exist, religious contradictions, skepticism, rationalism, evolution and religion, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Don't forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share.

comments.text:
Well put. What you've articulated in this video resonates strongly with my own journey of nearly three decades spent critically examining religious doctrine and belief systems. Much like you describe, the "divine ledger", as I often call it, was riddled with inconsistencies substantial enough to warrant a qualified opinion on whether it presented a true and fair view at all.

What followed was the gradual unpacking of a realisation that had been quietly present for years: faith had never truly occupied a meaningful place in my life. The surprising part was not becoming an atheist, but recognising that I apparently always had been one.

I eventually turned to science for answers. Yet, looking back, the shift did not begin there. It started much earlier through the examination of religion itself. My fascination with the scientific method came later; the questions that led to my conclusions about the insubstantiality of faith had already been asked.

Thoughtful, articulate content like this is increasingly rare. Looking forward to seeing more.

* contradicting things can't exist

* So God can't exist.

With other gods, it's not so cut and dry. THey're non-evidenced nonsense, so we shouldn't believe in any of them, but unless there's a contradiction it's basically not possible to fully disprove them. (But again: we don't need to.
